known_gaps: Catalogs are synthetic content; desktop drawn surfaces require human review
labwc reports no window geometry: toplevels are placed only by their own pixels (grim -T against the composed outputs); layer-shell surfaces of the shell are never placed

focus.reason: labwc has no IPC or geometry protocol: the toplevel lists give the active window, and each toplevel is placed and hit-tested by finding its own ext-foreign-toplevel capture in the composed outputs (probe toplevel-pixels); labwc does not raise a window put.gd shows while another client is active, so each guarded input first activates the target through its wlr handle

notifications.reason: Budgie's notification popups are budgie-daemon layer-shell surfaces: AT-SPI shows the showing summary label, and labwc reports no position for a layer surface

compositor.stage: none: grim (in the golden) and the shipped tools/lab/wayland_toplevels.py witness, read-only per observation

evidence.note: Live/sensitive frames: banner areas of this desktop's notification server (top and bottom positions) are always masked; in declared desktop frames non-owned windows other than browsers and the shell's own processes are masked, browser chrome is masked from live window geometry, and window-list panels only when a window title carries a link or registered value.

consent.reason: Budgie on labwc records through ext-image-copy-capture on put.gd's own connection; the ScreenCast portal is never used, so no consent dialog shows
